inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (+ VisualCoreTestSupport for test targets). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio, VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For Digital Zen Garden (checked 2026-11-17): VisualCoreScenes has PointerEvent, PointerTracker (10 pointers), the gesture recognizers and GestureArbiter, PointerVelocityTracker (uniform linear resampling, at most 16 samples per update), HeightField, GradientNoise2D, FractalNoise2D, SceneNode.hitTest and drawList, Primitive.contains and Mesh.revolution, extrusion and bevelledBox; VisualCoreRendering has RenderHost.pointerHandler, ResourceRegistry.makeRenderTarget (rgba8, rgba16f, r8), RenderTarget.readFloatPixels, PingPongTarget, FieldPass, FloatRenderSupport, TrailLayer, CachedScene, MeshRenderer, DepthMeshPass and ShaderBundle with the vc/ GLSL library; VisualCoreMath has Mat3; VisualCoreSimulation has SceneClock, AccessibilityPreferences and AnnouncementPlanner; VisualCoreExperience has ExperienceControl.maxValues (24), ExperienceInput.normalized, GestureAlternatives, ExperienceSnapshot, StateDigest, MigrationExample, ExperienceStorage and StorageQuota; VisualCorePersistence has MigrationChain; VisualCoreAudio has SoundEffectPlayer; VisualCoreExperienceHost has ExperienceFeedback; VisualCoreUI has SystemAccessibilityObserver. Missing in every framework product (grep 2026-11-17): coalesced or predicted touch samples, stroke smoothing, a brush-stamp pass into a height target, GLSL normal-from-height or lighting helpers, shadows, an undo or command stack, a named-document store over ExperienceStorage and a selection helper.

inventory.area: EGL render host and its main-thread rule
inventory.description: RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend (EGLDisplayProvider), the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler (CADisplayLink paced by FramePacing: 30 fps floor, lower caps under Low Power Mode or heat, else the presenter's maxFramesPerSecond, 60 by default) and context generations; every GL call runs on the main thread inside RenderScene setup, resize, render and teardown. RenderHost, RenderScene, the presenter, the shell and the action port are main-actor; the core is a Sendable value advanced in fixed steps (ExperienceEngine.advance(frame:)) that never reads a clock or draws. RenderHost pauses in the background, resumes in the foreground, and rebuilds on memory warning and recreateContext.

inventory.area: Shaders and resources (full-screen shaders, fields, persistent and ping-pong render targets, meshes)
inventory.description: FullScreenShaderScene draws one bundled fragment shader over the canvas; FieldPass runs a fragment program into a render target or the framebuffer, and over a PingPongTarget (read and write targets swapped per step, invalid after context loss) for feedback; ResourceRegistry.makeRenderTarget creates rgba8, rgba16f or r8 targets under a ResourceBudget; FloatRenderSupport probes half-float rendering per context generation and falls back to rgba8; RenderTarget.readPixels and readFloatPixels read targets back for tests; TrailLayer keeps a decaying trail; ShaderBundle and ShaderLibrary compile bundled GLSL with #include of the vc/ library (palette, noise, sdf, hash, colour, field; no lighting or normal-from-height helper); Mesh.revolution, extrusion and bevelledBox build procedural meshes drawn by MeshRenderer (one directional light) or DepthMeshPass; CachedScene keeps a still frame.

RenderView+Touches turns UITouch events into PointerEvent values with stable touch ids and timestamps (one position per touch event; no coalesced or predicted samples) and hands them to RenderHost.pointerHandler; the experience host routes them to ExperiencePresenter.pointer(_:viewSize:port:) and cancelPointers; PointerTracker keeps at most 10 pointers, the recognizers (tap, double tap, long press, drag, pinch, rotate) and GestureArbiter decide gestures, PointerVelocityTracker resamples a path to uniform spacing with a cap; ExperienceInput.normalized maps view points to canvas coordinates and ExperienceInput.validate checks actions of at most ExperienceControl.maxValues (24) values before the core sees them; GestureAlternatives.missing lists gestures without a native control.

AccessibilityPreferences resolves Reduce Motion and Reduce Flashing against the system (observed by SystemAccessibilityObserver); AnnouncementPlanner rate-limits announcements; SceneClock.reducedMotionFactor slows animation; ExperienceFeedback routes haptics (silent when the person's switch is off) and announcements; SoundEffectPlayer plays procedural one-shot SoundEffects in the ambient session category with no permission (isEnabled defaults to true).

ExperienceSnapshot (at most 1 MiB, checksum, schema version) with StateDigest; MigrationChain migrates payloads forward and MigrationExample registers stored examples per schema; ExperienceStorage is the experience's own folder and values under StorageQuota (16 MiB, 64 files); DocumentStore and NamedLibrary take a directory URL. No named-document store over ExperienceStorage exists; Fractal Explorer's FractalBookmarks and Ambient Clock's AmbientFavourites are experience-local.

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies quality (QualityGovernor over the QualityProfile, fed by DeviceConditions), memory-warning and scene-phase events and keeps a PerformanceRecord; ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls, pointer input, canvas overlay through makeCanvasOverlay); ExperienceCore is the GPU-free state with its qualityTiers; the one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json (nineteen registered, A01-A19, candidates empty, checked 2026-11-17; Digital Zen Garden joins in A20-P01 and stays unregistered and unavailable in A20-P00; scripts/check_experience_packages.py forbids unregistered targets).

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: 153 named steps listed by --list on 2026-11-17 (shared checks including app-contracts, which checks every docs/apps/*/visualcore-contract.json, licenses and usage-descriptions; package and app builds and tests; experience-release and copy-claims steps of the released experiences; verify steps of A01-A19 on iOS 27 and 26; the app's release audits; the seven reference regression steps and the ProjectM independence check). No A20 step exists yet; the A20 copy-claims and verify steps come with G-RELEASE.

Digital Zen Garden owns its domain (the garden document with strokes, stones and the command log, caps and schema; stroke resampling, smoothing and the two rake footprints; undo and redo by command; the sand stamp pass, relief and shadow shaders and the replay from checkpoints; the stone palette, placement and layer-aware selection; named gardens; the low-stimulation mode; copy) and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/DigitalZenGarden/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests, Shaders, scenario-manifest.json; created in A20-P01, not present today). VisualCore owns reusable machinery: touch input and gestures (VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreScenes), render targets, fields, the GLSL library and meshes (VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreScenes), animation clocks and accessibility planning (VisualCoreSimulation), persistence (VisualCorePersistence), storage, snapshots and the host (VisualCoreExperience, VisualCoreExperienceHost), sound (VisualCoreAudio). Light Maze's undo, Fractal Explorer's bookmarks, Ambient Clock's favourites, Fluid Art Playground's splats and the pickers of other experiences stay experience code and are not copied. ProjectM stays in the harness.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in docs/apps/digital-zen-garden/regression-baseline.md.

StateDigest fingerprints the core state so the same command log gives the same digest; ScenarioManifest and ScenarioRunner replay recorded steps; QualityProfile levels and QualityGovernor with FramePacing step quality and frame cap down under heat and Low Power Mode; ResourceBudget bounds GPU bytes; PointerTracker, PointerVelocityTracker, ExperienceSnapshot.maxBytes and StorageQuota bound input and storage.

gaps.justification: The garden document (tray, strokes, stones, the command log in normalized tray coordinates), its caps, validation and schema are the experience's domain, GPU-free in its Core (manual phase 01).
gaps.test: Core host tests: documents round-trip and migrate; truncated, newer, NaN, infinite and out-of-range input refused; caps on samples per stroke, strokes and stones enforced; every action stays within 24 values

gaps.justification: Stroke resampling to uniform spacing with a cap, smoothing and the two rake footprints are pure math over PointerVelocityTracker's samples; they are specific to raking. No VisualCore change is planned (spec clarification Q4); a second user would justify moving it upstream later (Principle II).
gaps.test: Core host tests: a fast drag resampled at the declared spacing leaves no gap; the cap is counted, not exceeded; smoothing keeps endpoints; each rake style gives its footprint fixture

gaps.justification: No undo or command stack exists in VisualCore; Light Maze's is experience-local. The garden's undo/redo is by command over its log, never by texture snapshot (research D6). No VisualCore change is planned (spec clarification Q4); a second user would justify moving it upstream later (Principle II).
gaps.test: Core host tests: undo and redo of strokes and stone edits restore the earlier digest; redo cleared by a new command; the log cap holds; fixtures for each command kind

gaps.justification: The sand height target (rgba16f through FloatRenderSupport, rgba8 fallback) on a PingPongTarget with the experience's stamp FieldPass, and its replay from the nearest checkpoint after undo, redo, restore, resize or context loss (manual phase 02). No brush-stamp pass exists in VisualCore. No VisualCore change is planned (spec clarification Q4); a second user would justify moving it upstream later (Principle II). It also sends each stroke to the core as small actions within ExperienceControl.maxValues (the transport part of M12), with the experience in A20-P02. As built (A20-P02, spec clarification Q1): the strokes are stamped on the CPU into a 480 × 360 SandField and uploaded with RenderTarget.upload(rgbaFloats:) to one rgba16f target (rgba8 fallback), because FieldUniform carries no arrays and a GPU stamp pass would cost a full-target pass per sample; the GPU draws the relief.
gaps.test: Experience tests: replaying a log gives the same read-back heights (readFloatPixels) as drawing it live; after context loss or resize the target is rebuilt and equal; the rgba8 fallback is exercised; checkpoints bound replay length

gaps.justification: Normal-from-height and soft lighting of the sand are experience shaders over vc/; no lighting helper exists in the GLSL library. No VisualCore change is planned (spec clarification Q4); a second user would justify moving it upstream later (Principle II).
gaps.test: Experience tests: a known height fixture lights to the expected brightness range; the shader compiles through ShaderBundle; no flashing between frames; license inventory lists the shader

gaps.justification: The brush preview ring and the brush zoom for small screens are the experience's interface over the canvas overlay (manual risk 2).
gaps.test: Experience tests: the preview follows the pointer and matches the footprint size; the zoom keeps strokes in tray coordinates; the preview never changes the state

gaps.justification: The stone palette as procedural shapes, and placement, rotation and deletion in normalized tray coordinates independent of orientation, are the experience's domain (manual phase 03). As built (A20-P03, spec clarification Q1): stones are superellipse domes from the pure StoneShape, rasterized in depth order into a 480 × 360 StoneLayer and uploaded as a second target of the one relief pass, instead of meshes through a second depth-tested pass.

gaps.justification: Layer-aware selection over SceneNode.hitTest and drawList, with a non-colour selection mark, is experience code; no selection helper exists in VisualCore. negative.rule: Risk 1, GPU feedback undo can be expensive. Owner: the command log and undo semantics (app-local G-UNDO and G-DOCUMENT in A20-P01) and the sand replay from checkpoints (G-SAND in A20-P02). Verification: Core tests prove undo and redo restore the earlier digest by command; experience tests prove a replay from the nearest checkpoint gives the same read-back heights as live drawing and that checkpoints bound the replay length; a source scan finds no texture snapshot kept for undo. Release blocker: undo implemented by texture snapshots, a replay that differs from live drawing, or an unbounded replay or checkpoint memory.

Risk 2, touch precision at small sizes. Owner: stroke resampling (app-local G-STROKES in A20-P01), the brush preview and brush zoom (G-PREVIEW in A20-P02) and the device measurements (G-DEVICE in A20-P05, with the coalesced-touch assessment). Verification: Core tests prove a fast drag leaves no gap at the declared spacing; experience tests prove the preview matches the footprint and the zoom keeps tray coordinates; the device campaign records precision on the smallest phone. Release blocker: a gap in a fast stroke, no brush zoom or preview, or a precision or latency claim not measured on a device.

Risk 3, bright effects disrupting calm. Owner: the low-stimulation mode and quiet defaults (app-local G-QUIET in A20-P05), the relief and shadow shaders (G-RELIEF, G-SHADOWS) and the accessibility work (G-A11Y in A20-P04). Verification: tests prove a new garden starts with sound and animation off, Reduce Motion stops animation and Reduce Flashing is honoured, and no frame-to-frame brightness jump exceeds the declared limit; the device campaign verifies the quiet defaults. Release blocker: sound or animation on by default, any flash, or Reduce Motion or Reduce Flashing ignored.

reasons: A working host and touch path exist: RenderHost on OpenGL ES -> ANGLE -> Metal (main-actor) draws any RenderScene, and RenderHost.pointerHandler delivers multi-touch PointerEvents with stable ids and timestamps to ExperiencePresenter.pointer and cancelPointers, resampled to uniform spacing with a cap by PointerVelocityTracker, all public and tested (TouchAdapterTests, PointerPathTests, PointerCancelTests, PointerVelocityTrackerTests).

A persistent drawable target exists: ResourceRegistry.makeRenderTarget with rgba16f through FloatRenderSupport (rgba8 fallback), PingPongTarget and FieldPass, with float read-back for tests, as Simulation Lab and Fluid Art Playground use (PingPongTargetTests, FieldPassTests, FloatRenderSupportTests).

Storage exists: ExperienceSnapshot with StateDigest and MigrationChain, and ExperienceStorage under StorageQuota (ExperienceSnapshotTests, ExperienceStorageTests); procedural meshes, 2D transforms with depth-ordered hit testing, a cached still frame, sound and haptics are public and tested.

11 of 31 rows are available with tests; all 20 non-available rows have owned app-local gaps: G-DOCUMENT, G-STROKES and G-UNDO in A20-P01; G-SAND, G-RELIEF and G-PREVIEW in A20-P02; G-STONES, G-SELECTION and G-SHADOWS in A20-P03; G-LIBRARY and G-A11Y in A20-P04; G-QUIET and G-DEVICE in A20-P05; G-RELEASE in A20-P06. No VisualCore change is needed to start (spec clarification Q4).

No permission is needed (sound is an ambient one-shot player). Digital Zen Garden stays unregistered (19 registered, A01-A19) until A20-P01 creates Packages/ExperiencesCreative/DigitalZenGarden with its targets and first real rules.
